_comment: Worked-example constants and phrases the prompt templates substitute, all read off the real library (Econometrics/Identification/PotentialOutcomes.lean). `exemplar` is `condMean`, the def every identification statement in the library is an equation between — the right thing to show a drafter as 'consume this, do not re-derive it'. `exemplar_partial` is the same def under-applied, which in this library is the LIVE pitfall: `condMean` takes three explicit arguments and a two-argument application is a `(Ω → ℝ) → ℝ` where a real was wanted.
exemplar_grounded_bodies: a Bochner integral, ProbabilityTheory.cond, Set.indicator, an existing Econometrics estimand
exemplar_piecewise: an estimand branching on treatment status or on a period
exemplar_provable_side_condition: a conditional mean built from `∫ … ∂(μ[|s])` is already defined when `μ s = 0` (the conditioned measure is zero and the integral is `0`), so an explicit `μ s ≠ 0` hypothesis is unnecessary
